Maya: heads-up — noticed a perf regression on a subset of infra after the kernel-path tweak in the last runtime rollout. median latency for seq=64 spiked ~25% on some nodes. digging into profiler now. commit d4c2b9a
Liam: which nodes? fleet or a single instance type?
Maya: mostly our eu-rt-2 pool (A10x-ish machines). felt like kernel selection picked a slower matmul path for mid sequences. exact sample:
```
kernel chosen: matmul_tiled_sm89_opt_v2  time=4.8ms
kernel fallback: matmul_generic_v1      time=2.9ms
seq=64, batch=4, kv_cache_enabled=true
```
Maya: looks like the "sm-capability fingerprint" returned a slightly different capability flags on these hosts, which pushed routing into the tiled path that ends up being slower for our seqlen distribution.
Arjun: can you dump the device probe output (hw_sig / sm_major / tensor_cores / bf16_fp8 flags)? might be driver-reported quirk.
Maya: pasted probe:
```
GPU 0: device_name=Radeon-like? (weird shim) hw_sig=0x5b3 sm=89 driver=538.1
cap_flags: tensor_cores=1 bf16=1 fp8=0 fp8_beta=0
heuristic_pick: prefer_tiled_when_tensorcore=1
```
Ciara: driver 538 is old-ish for that SKU — we had a vendor patched shim that misreports fp8 support on some kernels. fp8 detection fallback logic is brittle.
Maya: perf-bot shows a correlated spike in token tail latency at 2026-03-05T14:12 (deploy time) — ~30% regressing relative to baseline on eu-rt-2 only.
perf-bot: [automated alert] metric=latency_p95 service=runtime model=vicuna-13b route=/generate delta=+30% threshold=+10% window=1h link=https://perf.internal/alerts/1234 :warning:
Liam: so two separate issues: (1) hw probe misreporting FP8/tensor capabilities, (2) heuristic prefers tiled kernel when tensor_cores=1 but tiled is worse for seq=64 in many cases. we should gate the tiled-path with a sequencing-aware rule.
Arjun: +1. suggest heuristic: if (sm_major==89 && driver < 540) then ignore fp8/tensor_reporting for routing; and add a microbench check on first N inferences to verify tiled actually wins before committing route. pseudo: 
```
if hw.sm_major == 89 and hw.driver_version < 540:
  route_policy.force_probe_microbench = true
  window=50 samples
  choose kernel with lower mean latency for observed seq distribution
```
Ciara: also add a kv_cache warmup check — current kv eviction pattern combined with tiled path causes extra memcopies. beam/long-context workloads hit thrash. short-term we can disable prefetched tiled tiling for kv_enabled=true on that hw sig.
Maya: I can try a canary patch that (a) forces microbench probe and (b) disables tiled-prefetch when kv_enabled on that hw_sig. anyone want to run the canary?
Liam: I will run canary on two eu-rt-2 nodes and one us-rt-1 node for control.
Arjun: will draft a minimal patch, keeping telemetry so we can audit kernel picks per request. snippet for runtime flag: 
```json
{"kernel_heuristics": {"sm89_driver_lt_540": {"force_probe": true, "disable_tiled_when_kv": true}}}
```
Maya: pushed build with env REDWOOD_CANARY=kernel-sm89-20260305 and extra logging to stackdriver. rolling to two nodes now.
perf-bot: [canary-deploy] rollout to eu-rt-2-node-17, eu-rt-2-node-19 status=running
Liam: initial numbers after ~2000 requests: p95 down ~18% vs regression peak, overall median restored to baseline. sending longer run.
Ciara: file a short postmortem item to add a unit-test for the hw probe parser + a microbench gate before committing kernel path. we'll also coordinate with HW vendor to validate driver reports.
Maya: will open PR and add TODOs. thanks all :thumbsup:
Arjun: note for follow-up — we should extend device fingerprint to include driver build id and add a TTL so old cached fingerprints don't persist across driver upgrades.
Maya: +1. creating task in backlog: INF-1913 (hw-fingerprint-ttl + microbench gating).
Liam: nice catch, Maya. marking this thread resolved once canary finishes. :white_check_mark:
